method: Open opportunities identified by checking Measure's top-ranked funders for current cycles, plus targeted discovery across racial equity / community-led data, nonprofit capacity building, ethical AI governance, and criminal justice reform. Each listing was deduplicated by URL and verified.
known_limitation: Open-grant opportunities are a point-in-time snapshot from public research. Confirm each program's current cycle, deadline, and eligibility on the funder's own website before applying.

ready_now.amount: Not specified; caps contribution at ~10% of org's annual operating budget, ~25% of project budget
ready_now.eligibility: Nonprofits serving urban low-income communities in Texas (or other listed regions); no individuals, medical research, lobbying, or hardware
ready_now.focus_area: Quality Schools, Jobs & Livelihoods, Health Innovation, Strong Communities
ready_now.notes: Measure's racial-equity/data-justice/AI-governance focus isn't a clean match to Dell's stated categories -- 'Strong Communities' or 'Other' likely closest fit. Since this is a confirmed prior funder ($131,000 already given), the existing relationship likely opens a warmer path than the cold portal.

ready_now.deadline: Rolling (one request per 12 months); two named funds have a firm July 31, 2026 deadline (Hispanic Impact Fund $22k-$55.5k, Women's Fund $20k-$60k)
ready_now.amount: Discretion of individual fundholders; ACF advises requesting no more than 30% of annual operating budget
ready_now.notes: Confirmed prior funder. The two named July 31 funds (Hispanic Impact, Women's) are partial fits if Measure frames its equity/data-justice research around those specific populations -- not a clean match for the core public-safety-data/AI-governance work.

ready_now.deadline: Rolling; interest form, not a formal cycle
ready_now.focus_area: General social impact, civic/nonprofit capacity building; related Notley Tide program focuses on racial justice work in Central Texas
ready_now.notes: New top-ranked candidate (see funder_match_ranked_v1.json, #3). Not a guaranteed process -- Notley states high demand means not all requests get a response. Worth also checking Notley's other programs (Philanthropitch, Notley Fellowship, Notley Tide) separately, which have their own distinct processes.

ready_now.grant_name: General Grantmaking; Racial Equity Program Area
ready_now.deadline: Rolling; LOI required via Fluxx portal, ~30 business day response
ready_now.amount: Varies; typically multi-year, multi-hundred-thousand-dollar community initiatives
ready_now.eligibility: 501(c)(3) nonprofits nationally; Texas is outside WKKF's named priority geographies (Michigan, Mississippi, New Mexico, New Orleans)
ready_now.focus_area: Equity and healing from systemic racism; community-driven solutions
ready_now.notes: Real, open, non-invitation-only pathway via LOI -- but Texas competes in the general pool, not a priority geography. Worth confirming current fit with a program officer before investing LOI-writing time.

ready_now.deadline: Rolling within an annual cycle; board meets 5x/year (Jan/Apr/Jun/Sep/Nov); apply 4+ months ahead; one proposal per org per 12 months
ready_now.amount: Not published; typically tens of thousands to low hundreds of thousands
ready_now.eligibility: 501(c)(3) benefiting people of Texas (org need not be TX-headquartered)
ready_now.focus_area: Civic & Public Affairs (one of five funding areas); explicitly seeks 'quantitatively measurable outcomes'
ready_now.notes: No racial-equity-specific fund, but the explicit preference for measurable-outcomes proposals is a genuine natural fit for Measure's data/evaluation and nonprofit-governance capacity work -- frame around data/evaluation capacity, not equity-labeling.

ready_now.deadline: Rolling; unsolicited inquiry submitted anytime, response (invite or decline) in ~3 months
ready_now.amount: Not fixed; has made grants up to $20M across a portfolio, individual grants commonly tens of thousands to low millions
ready_now.eligibility: 501(c)(3) serving greater Houston/Harris County and contiguous counties
ready_now.focus_area: Civic Engagement (one of four priorities); prior $20M dedicated to anti-Black-racism/systemic-injustice work in Houston
ready_now.notes: Full applications are invitation-only, but unsolicited inquiries are the real entry point (up to 5 declines allowed before being barred from resubmitting). Geographic constraint is key: Measure's Houston office would need genuine local programmatic presence, not just Austin HQ work, to qualify.

ready_now.deadline: Rolling; pre-applications reviewed continuously, decisions announced January and July
ready_now.eligibility: 501(c)(3) serving Harris, Travis, or Walker County, TX; once per year per org
ready_now.focus_area: Education, Arts, Conservation, Human Services; general operating costs eligible
ready_now.notes: Travis County (Austin) is an explicit geographic priority. General operating support can cover organizational/governance capacity work, though 'capacity building' isn't named as its own category -- frame within operating-support or human-services.

ready_now.amount: Drawn from a $50M 2026 commitment; prior round averaged ~$100K-$500K per org
ready_now.focus_area: Community-led engagement with AI to reduce barriers, expand opportunity, elevate community voice
ready_now.notes: Direct thematic match to Measure's ethical-AI-governance/community-voice work. DEADLINE IS VERY CLOSE (about a week from the research date) -- verify Measure's operating budget falls in the $500K-$10M band immediately if pursuing this.

ready_now.amount: $100,000-$300,000 per award, multi-year (2-year); at least $3.5M total in 2026
ready_now.eligibility: 501(c)(3) or international equivalent; must register in Fluxx 24+ hours before deadline
ready_now.focus_area: Public-interest cybersecurity infrastructure, protecting civil society/journalists online
ready_now.notes: Adjacent, not direct -- best framed as support for Measure's data-security/data-stewardship practices rather than its core AI-ethics research. 2026 geographic priority favors 'global majority' orgs, a competitive disadvantage for a U.S./Texas applicant despite formal eligibility.

ready_now.organization: The Just Trust (and The Just Trust for Action)
ready_now.amount: Varies; typically multi-year general operating support, tens of thousands to low hundreds of thousands
ready_now.eligibility: 501(c)(3) working on U.S. criminal justice reform; no state restriction
ready_now.focus_area: Advocacy infrastructure, media/narrative projects, justice alternatives, rapid response
ready_now.notes: Best thematic fit found for Measure's public-safety-metrics focus -- but The Just Trust states it's 'intentionally selective' and no longer proactively solicits unsolicited proposals. Treat the rolling inquiry as a relationship-building entry point, not a guaranteed competitive call.

ready_now.grant_name: Kapor Foundation Grantmaking (Governance / Innovation); open Letter of Inquiry
ready_now.deadline: Rolling, no fixed cycle; online LOI form
ready_now.amount: Not standardized; historically tens of thousands to low hundreds of thousands per grantee
ready_now.eligibility: U.S. 501(c)(3); prioritizes California/Oakland, Detroit, Atlanta, but nationwide LOIs accepted
ready_now.focus_area: Governance: algorithmic bias, AI safeguards, surveillance/civil rights, tech policy at the intersection of racial equity and technology
ready_now.notes: RECOVERED from a matching-bug false-rejection (see known_limitation above) -- the underlying research is solid and this is a strong direct thematic match for Measure's data-justice/algorithmic-accountability work. Expect a competitive/longer-shot fit given the hub-city priority, but Texas orgs are not excluded.

watch_list_not_yet_open.why_watch: Directly matches Measure's community-led data/evaluation mission in RWJF's own program language ($50,000/grant, up to 30 awards) -- but the 2026 round closed March 3, 2026. Recurring program; monitor RWJF's active-opportunities page for the next cycle.

The only Central-Texas funder found that names 'capacity building' explicitly as a fundable use. 2026 cycle closed Feb 5, 2026; strong recurring annual pattern suggests a ~January 2027 reopening, though not yet confirmed/announced.

watch_list_not_yet_open.organization: Humanity AI (pooled fund of 10 foundations incl. Ford, MacArthur, Mellon, Mozilla)
watch_list_not_yet_open.why_watch: A ~$10M open call (first broadly competitive round of a $500M/5-year coalition) explicitly prioritizing community-led groups -- a strong potential future match. But as of the research date, no application mechanics, LOI process, or exact opening date exist yet. Sign up on humanityai.ai for the announcement.

watch_list_not_yet_open.organization: U.S. DOJ; National Institute of Justice / Bureau of Justice Statistics
watch_list_not_yet_open.grant_name: FY 2026 State and Local Collection and Reporting of Crime Data
watch_list_not_yet_open.why_watch: The single most on-theme match by title (public safety data/accountability), genuinely open (Grants.gov deadline July 30, 2026), but eligibility is unconfirmed for a standalone 501(c)(3) -- this program lineage has historically been restricted to state/local government leads. Pull the full NOFO's 'Eligible Applicants' section before investing time; likely path is as a named subrecipient/data-analysis partner to a government lead, not direct application.

Best-matched 'accountability data/ethical AI' funder found, but the specific Data Practice Accelerator program is confirmed archived/not accepting applications. Open cycles rotate themes -- worth monitoring for a reopened call to pitch a data-justice/racial-equity-data proposal via LOI.

Explicit past Texas eligibility and a direct thematic match (reducing incarceration, racial/gender disparities), but most recent confirmed round dates to 2020-2021; no evidence of a current or announced 2025-2026 cycle. Targeted at small-city/rural communities specifically, a real geographic mismatch with Measure's Austin/Houston/Dallas metro focus. Verify status directly via Vera's Submittable portal.
